name: Mairenn

attributes.attribute: an Irish heroine and a wife of a king of Tara who always wore a gold headdress
the co-wife who envied Mairenn's jewelry and suspected she was hiding something
bald beneath the gold headdress, revealed when a bribed jester pulled it off
cursed Mugain, and golden locks then covered her own head in the same moment
forced to bear a lamb and a salmon before giving birth to a human child

sources: MacNeill, Máire. "The Festival of Lughnasa, Parts I and II." Dublin: Comhairle Bhéaloideas Éireann, 1982. 326-327.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Mairenn was an Irish heroine. A king of Tara had two wives. One of them, Mairenn, always wore a gorgeous headdress of gold. The other wife, Mugain, was envious of her co-wife's jewelry and suspected Mairenn was hiding something. She was right, for Mairenn was bald beneath the gold. A bribed woman jester yanked the headdress off Mairenn's head. Mairenn cursed Mugain, but even as she did so, splendid golden locks covered her head so no one saw her shame. Because of her ill will, Mugain was forced to bear a lamb and a salmon before she could give birth to a child.

okr.objective: Document Mairenn, the bald Irish heroine whose golden headdress hid her secret.
